## How GRACE Follow-On Tracks Changes in Earth’s Mass

GRACE Follow-On consists of two satellites that follow one another about 137 miles (220 kilometers) apart. The distance between them is the measurement at the center of the mission’s study of shifting mass on Earth.

As the satellites approach a larger concentration of mass, its stronger gravity acts on the leading satellite first, initially pulling it farther from the trailing satellite. The changing separation is a raw measurement that scientists use to infer shifts in mass on Earth.

Those inferred shifts help scientists investigate changes in groundwater, lakes and rivers, soil moisture, glaciers and ice sheets. The measurements also help investigate sea-level changes attributable to water added to the oceans.
